_comment: The single source for both matrices. ost-compare --matrix renders it and
the README's tables are generated from it, so the two cannot drift.
Cell values: yes | no | part | unknown.
yes     observed by running the tool, or read directly in its source
no      observed absent by running it, or absent from its source
part    present but incomplete, or claimed by a README and not verified
unknown could not be determined; the note says what was checked
Every cell that is not yes or no carries a note. See docs/method.md.
snapshotNote: Every tool is built from a revision pinned in flake.lock. Run `nix eval --json .#lib.versions` for the exact set.

tools.blurb: Finds every OpenSpec project on disk and reports status across all of them. The only tool here whose unit is the machine rather than one project.
A reader for one project, parsing the filesystem directly. The most finished of the six: tabbed artifacts, rendered markdown, filtering, and task toggling.
Not a reader. It runs changes: batch execution, a dependency graph between them, a configurable agent command, and an in-app config editor.
An authoring front end. Its opening screen offers creating a change, opening one, and listing them. Three commits, and its README points at a different repository.
The only tool that drives the openspec CLI JSON API instead of parsing files, which is why it is also the only one with --store. Validate, archive and task toggling from inside the interface.
The widest ambition: a Kanban board, an agent runner with its own logs and runs views, settings, and diagnostics. Eight commits, and the README reads as a roadmap.

features.label: Runs an agent to implement a change

properties.label: Needs the openspec CLI at runtime
Starts with no OpenSpec root in sight

notes.collision: Three upstream projects install a binary with this name. They cannot coexist on one PATH, which is why this flake exposes ost- prefixed names instead.
notes.not-consumed: Upstream ships a flake, but this repo takes it as a flake = false input anyway, so packaging stays uniform across all six.
notes.glamour: Uses the glamour markdown renderer, present in go.mod.
notes.tui-markdown: Uses tui-markdown with the highlight-code feature, declared in Cargo.toml.
notes.watchfiles: Declares watchfiles as a dependency in pyproject.toml.
notes.specgetty-no-markdown: go.mod declares no markdown renderer: the dependencies are bubbletea, bubbles, lipgloss, godirwalk, urfave/cli and yaml.
notes.specgetty-aggregate: Source aggregates task statistics across changes, so the progress it reports is per project rather than per change.
notes.specgetty-archive: Source carries an archive flow with idle, confirming and running states. Not exercised in this comparison.
notes.specgetty-rescan: The README documents `s` to rescan, which is a manual refresh rather than a watcher.
notes.specgetty-path: --path selects a project and --zoom starts inside it. The unit is a project, not a change.
notes.specgetty-scan: Scanning the disk for every OpenSpec project is the tool's purpose.
notes.specgetty-no-filter-key: No filter or search key appears in the README key table, and no filter string was found in the source. Not confirmed absent.
notes.specgetty-no-help-key: No help key appears in the README key table. --help works from the command line. An in-interface overlay was not confirmed either way.
notes.dossier-keys: From the README key table: Space toggles the task under the cursor on the tasks tab, and `e` opens the artifact in $EDITOR.
notes.dossier-filter: Filter mode is confirmed in the source, which tests entering it with `/`, cancelling with Esc and confirming with Enter.
notes.dossier-path: --help shows an optional [path] argument. A change directory passed directly must contain .openspec.yaml.
notes.dossier-reload: A handful of watcher-shaped references appear in the source, too few to call it either way without running a file-change test.
notes.dossier-statusbar: The interface carries a persistent status line listing keys rather than a dismissable overlay.
notes.neosam-specs: The source mentions specs extensively, but this tool's screens are organised around changes and runs. Not confirmed either way.
notes.neosam-batch: Batch execution is the most heavily represented feature in the source, together with an explicit Add Dependency action between changes.
notes.neosam-agent: The configurable command defaults to variants of `claude`, including `claude --print --dangerously-skip-permissions {prompt}`.
notes.neosam-config: A Config screen with an edit mode is present in the source, backed by a config.yaml.
notes.neosam-archive: An Archived tab exists for browsing. Whether a change can be archived from the interface was not confirmed.
notes.neosam-filter: Some filter-shaped references appear in the source, too few to call it either way.
notes.neosam-no-args: The tool parses no arguments at all. Without a terminal it exits 1 with ENXIO from opening /dev/tty.
notes.neosam-no-help-key: No help key was found in the source. Not confirmed absent.
notes.mstanton-scope: The observed opening screen offers creating a change, opening one, and listing them. Nothing about archives or specs appeared.
notes.mstanton-preview: A Preview binding exists on ctrl+p. Whether it renders markdown was not confirmed.
notes.mstanton-no-args: No argument parsing was found; the tool opens its interface immediately.
notes.mstanton-license: MIT is claimed in pyproject.toml and the README. There is no LICENSE file in the tree, and the GitHub API reports no license for the repository.
notes.itslame-keys: From the key table in the source: `/` filter, space toggle task, `e` edit in $EDITOR, `v` validate, `A` archive, `r` refresh, `?` help.
notes.itslame-cli: main.go calls exec.LookPath("openspec") before anything else and exits 1 with an install hint if it fails. All commands go through the CLI.
notes.itslame-store: --help documents `-store string`, an OpenSpec store id to use as the workspace root. This is the only tool of the six with it.
notes.itslame-path: --help documents a positional path argument: a directory containing an openspec/ root.
notes.itslame-refresh: `r` refreshes manually. No watcher was found.
notes.opsx-board: The interface opens on a Board tab with collapsible columns and a priority action.
notes.opsx-runner: Runner, Runs and Logs views exist. Whether an agent actually runs from them was not exercised.
notes.opsx-settings: A Settings view exists in the source.
notes.opsx-help: `?` is bound to a help screen.
notes.opsx-tasks-tab: A Tasks tab exists. No toggle or progress action was found in the bindings, so neither is confirmed.
notes.opsx-diagnostics: A Diagnostics view exists, which may or may not be validation. Not confirmed.
notes.opsx-edit-metadata: `e` edits metadata in the interface. Opening an external $EDITOR was not confirmed.
notes.opsx-filter: Filter-shaped references appear in the source but no filter key appears in the bindings.
notes.opsx-recent-projects: It remembers recently opened projects, but shows one project at a time.
notes.opsx-project: --help documents --project PROJECT, a path to an OpenSpec project root.
notes.opsx-silent-exit: With a clean HOME and no OpenSpec root in the working directory it exits 0 after 239 bytes, drawing nothing and printing no error. It does not walk up the way the CLI does.
notes.opsx-license: The tree carries a GPL-3.0 LICENSE file and GitHub reports GPL-3.0, but the README says the license has yet to be defined and that redistribution permission must not be assumed.
notes.archive-handling: Archive-shaped references appear in the source but no archive view appears in the tab list.
